note: What Sega printed about the cartridge header, fact by fact, with the sentence each one was read from. Where the cartridges do something else, divergences.json says so and says which one this package follows.

order: hardware.json, for anything Sega stated: where the header sits, the string it opens with, where the checksum is kept, and the size codes
Sega's boot programs, for what the code that reads a header actually checks, and the cartridges themselves, for what a retail image actually contains, which is not always what the manual describes
authority.why: The manual is a description for licensees, retyped by an unnamed hand, so a cartridge can disagree with it and still be genuine, and the boot program that reads a header is the last word on what it checks. Where either disagrees with the manual, divergences.json records which way this package went.

comparedAgainst.what: Every image in a real library, walked and measured, which is the artifact rather than a description of it.

referenceManual.publisher: Sega, by its own page footer
referenceManual.title: Software Reference Manual for the SEGA Mark III Console
referenceManual.note: A retyped text with a clean text layer, so every quote below was read from it directly. The page numbers are the ones its own footers print.

headerAddress.quote: The header format is as follows (addresses shown for 32 KByte and larger cartridges):

checksum.quote: A 16-bit checksum for the ROM (low-hi order). $7FFA and $7FFB are not included in this checksum.

serialNumber.quote: A 16-bit serial number, assigned by Sega.

notStated.otherRegions: Every size code the manual prints carries a high nibble of 4. The other region codes this package reads, 3 for a Japanese Master System and 5, 6 and 7 for the Game Gear, are not in it and rest on the census.
notStated.largerSizes: The largest size the manual prints is 256K. Low nibbles 1 and 2 are read as 512K and 1M because the export boot program's bank table counts 30 and 62 banks for them; divergences.json carries it.
notStated.whichBytesTheChecksumCovers: The manual leaves only the two checksum bytes out of the sum, which reproduces no stored value in the library. The package follows the span table and bank table of the export boot program instead, and divergences.json carries both measurements.
notStated.copierBlocks: A copier block is added by hardware Sega did not sell. The manual does not acknowledge it.
notStated.gameGear: The manual describes the Mark III and says nothing about the Game Gear.
